answer: When an agent moves between two federated organizations, its home identity provider issues a signed token that the partner verifies against the provider's published keys, and the token carries a one-time pulse of validity that dies after a single exchange. A Sybil minting a thousand fake agents cannot forge the provider's signature, because the relic of the home registry anchors every token, and the dune of invented identities collapses when the partner checks the exchange.
